lines.text: My logo's on every outfit I draw. Ralph Lauren had to sell shirts for that.
lines.note: Reacts to the TRMNL logo the figure wears in every drawing: the screen as a fashion house that got its branding for free.

lines.text: Monday gets the black tag. It seemed only respectful.
lines.note: Reacts to the black 'Tomorrow · Mon' tag as mourning dress; about the day, not the weather or the reader.

lines.text: Forecasters can say 'a mixed bag.' I have to draw an actual outfit.
lines.note: The screen's job against forecasters' hedging: a drawing can't be vague.

lines.text: My little figure works in every weather. Not one sick day yet.
lines.note: The figure as a model employee, workplace metaphor; true in every pool since some figure always shows.

lines.text: Somewhere a bride is reading tomorrow's forecast like a ransom note.
lines.note: Other people: the same nightly forecast is life or death to someone else; works for good and bad tomorrows alike.

lines.text: Most people read the weather like terms and conditions: skim, agree, regret.
lines.note: Other people's way of reading a forecast, in a familiar three-beat; about 'most people', not the reader.

lines.text: Michelangelo got a whole ceiling. I get tomorrow, and about this much room.
lines.note: The screen's job on a small screen, put next to the grandest commission; self-pity with a smug comparison.

lines.text: At midnight I turn back into a plain forecast. Cinderella at least got a ball.
lines.note: True to the screen (the evening view ends at midnight); the screen's big night is spent on weather.

lines.text: If the weather knew I was drawing it, it'd want its good side.
lines.note: The weather as a vain subject sitting for the screen's portrait; any weather.

lines.text: Somewhere a man is explaining the jet stream to someone who asked about dinner.
lines.note: Other people at this hour: the weather bore, with a specific evening detail.

lines.text: You assemble yourself from a drawing, like IKEA furniture. Same leftover screws.
lines.note: The reader really does dress from a little drawing; IKEA's figure-and-picture instructions, cruel twist that parts are missing.

lines.text: You take fashion advice from a black-and-white screen. It shows.
lines.note: The reader's whole style judged by its source; short and cruel about looks.

lines.text: You always read to the end in case it's a compliment. It's never a compliment.
lines.note: Catches the reader reading this very line; worth jab.

lines.text: My whole audience tonight is you. I've worked better rooms.
lines.note: The screen as a comic stuck with one bad crowd; true for the 8 pm to midnight window.

lines.text: I change my line every hour. You've had the same personality since high school.
lines.note: Uses the real hourly rotation of these lines against the reader's unchanging personality.

lines.text: Saturday, when you can look however you like. So, no change.
lines.note: The weekend dress-down license, which the reader has apparently been using all week.

lines.text: Checking the forecast is your best quality. I've looked for others.
lines.note: Backhanded praise for the very act of reading the screen; worth jab.

lines.text: You've looked at this outfit longer than anyone will look at you in it.
lines.note: Reacts to the reader studying tomorrow's drawing; cruel about how much attention they get.
